title: Settlement Basis for a Northbeam Returns and Restocking Refund
content:
The merchandise refund on a Northbeam Returns and Restocking authorisation is the line price times the units returned, times the percentage the schedule's grade ladder gives for the grade recorded, less the deductions for missing accessories, rounded to the cent. A refund is authorised, offset or paid out only while the authorisation stands inspected or settled. Sales tax is refunded in proportion to the merchandise actually refunded; the delivery charge, the installation charge and the recycling fee are refunded only where the schedule says so, and each is authorised as its own component so the customer can see what was and was not returned. *The restocking fee still outstanding is kept back from the refund as an offset rather than billed separately* — that clause is **no longer in force**, superseded by the current basis on which what is kept back is settled — and the refund never goes below nothing. The refund goes back by the method the schedule requires; where the schedule requires the original method and that method can no longer be credited, store credit is used on the schedules that allow the fallback and a bank transfer is arranged on those that do not. The money leaves the retailer within the schedule's settlement days counted in business days from the day the return was settled, and a business invoice credit appears within the schedule's invoice credit days.

## The merchandise figure, step by step

1. Take the line price and multiply it by the units returned.
2. Multiply that by the percentage the schedule's grade ladder gives for the grade recorded.
3. Take off the deductions for missing accessories.
4. Round to the cent.

The multiplication by the grade percentage is taken on the line price times the units, and the accessory deductions come off after it, not before.

## The state the authorisation must stand in

The status is read from the return authorisation record identified by its own reference number, together with the refund still outstanding on it, before the component is authorised, offset or paid. Only an authorisation standing inspected or settled admits any of the three; requested, authorized, in transit, received, denied and withdrawn do not.

## The components, one by one

| Component | When it is refunded |
| --- | --- |
| the merchandise | on the figure worked out above |
| sales tax | in proportion to the merchandise actually refunded |
| the delivery charge | only where the schedule says so |
| the installation charge | only where the schedule says so |
| the recycling fee | only where the schedule says so |

Each is authorised as its own component, so the customer can see what was and was not returned.

## The way back and the time it takes

Where the schedule requires the original method and that method can no longer be credited, store credit is used on the schedules that allow the fallback, and a bank transfer is arranged on the schedules that do not. The money leaves the retailer within the schedule's settlement days, counted in business days from the day the return was settled. A business invoice credit appears within the schedule's invoice credit days.
